newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN CEN.BANK DELAYS NEW LEU RATE COMPUTING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN CEN.BANK DELAYS NEW LEU RATE COMPUTING.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Monday it had postponed plans to launch a new method to compute the reference exchange rates for the leu currency. "The National Bank postpones its decision for a few days," a BNR statement said.

Last Tuesday, BNR said it would no longer compute the reference rate for the leu. It set Monday as deadline to announce a new method to compute the average rate, which it said should "reflect the reality on the interbank market."
The statement said the BNR's latest reference rate of 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed last Thursday, would remain valid until it would announce the new method.

"The postponement is caused by the fact that after the liberalising the foreign exchange market and abandonning the broker/dealer distinction the market has been the natural shocks triggered by such a change," the BNR statement said.

The reference rate, computed since August 1994 when the BNR introduced a free-floating foreign exchange market, was a weighted average based on daily reports of market operators. It was a guidance rate used for statistical accounting purposes.

Last week, the BNR restored local dealer licences to 24 banks, which act as market makers. Four banks which had rights to act as dealers under restrictions introduced by the former leftist government were allowed to keep their licences.
As a result trading revived on the interbank market, usually affected by chronic hard currency shortages.
Latest BNR data showed interbank trading amounted to $7.75 million last Friday, compared with a daily average of some $609,000 in January.
Dealers' quotes displayed by banks showed a variety of ranges over the past week, in stark contrast with the one-rate policy imposed by the four dealers in the past.
On Monday, dealers' quotes ranged from 8,750/900 to 9,100/200 to the dollar.
"Data show the market will calm down over the next days," the BNR statement said.
